modeReason: Three top stories independently clear the relevance threshold of 8 (the new flagship model release, record AI-driven earnings, and a judge's push for AI to decide court cases), so today opens a fresh narrative rather than continuing yesterday's chatbot-liability lawsuit story.
phrase: A tech company unveiled its smartest model yet, one most people still cannot use. A top judge says AI could soon start deciding real court cases instead.
phraseAlternatives: The newest flagship AI model is smarter than ever and still out of reach for most users. Meanwhile, a senior judge wants AI ruling on real court cases.
One company showed off a frontier model nobody outside the lab can touch. One judge wants a robot inside the courtroom, deciding actual cases.
Benchmarks keep climbing while public access keeps shrinking: the newest top model stays locked away. A top judge, meanwhile, wants AI judging real disputes.

brief.concept: A sleek new flagship AI model stands sealed inside a glass display case marked NEW with a NOT AVAILABLE tag on its door, while beside it a human judge leans down from the bench to hand a gavel to a small robot sitting in the courtroom dock.
brief.metaphor: The smartest model yet is on display, not in hand — and the hand reaching for real power belongs to a robot, not a person.
